### Fixed
- A post step that turns one skeletal mesh into another (such as Parametric outfit) no longer hides the original static mesh from the steps after it, so a clothing item made later in the chain gets its pickup mesh and icon again.

### Fixed
- Post-processing steps now receive the definition's main picture. A step that paints from the picture
  the mesh was made from was told there was none.

### Changed
- Copyright and licence notices now name Bojan Andrejek / MetaWorx LLC. It is still Apache 2.0, and nothing about how you may use it changed.

### Added
- **Skinned takes can be looked at in the Mesh tab.** The take list now holds skeletal meshes as well
  as static ones, so a garment that has been through a skinning step is no longer the one take of
  itself you could not see. The strip beneath says how many bones it has, and counts its triangles
  and vertices from the authored data rather than the render data, as it already did for a static
  mesh. Where a definition has made both, the skinned result is what opens — the same order the
  Content Browser tile uses.
- **An installed add-on can put its own control in the Mesh tab's bar**, and its own meshes beside
  the one on screen. MeshForge never reads what an add-on builds. The first is MeshForgeGarment's
  *Character*, which stands a body inside a garment.
- **Anything drawn beside the mesh puts the viewer into true space.** Left alone the viewer
  normalises — it centres each take on the origin and, comparing, turns and scales B to match A —
  which is right when the question is *which of these takes is better*. The moment something else is
  in the picture the question is *does this fit*, which is entirely about size and position, and
  every one of those adjustments becomes a lie. So then nothing is adjusted at all: every mesh is
  drawn at its own origin, at its own size, with its own pivot, exactly as a level would show them
  all dropped at 0, 0, 0. *Align* greys out with that as its reason, and the strip beneath reports
  each mesh's bounds centre and how much bigger B is than A — said, rather than fixed.
- **Post steps can be reordered.** Up and down arrows on each step move it with its settings and runs.
  The Post stage goes stale, since order changes what the chain makes; every output is kept. A move the
  chain could not run is not offered, and the greyed arrow says why.
- **Mesh Workflows**: a data asset that sets a definition up in one choice — which stages it uses,
  the pipeline on each and the post-processing chain, with their settings, and optionally its import
  settings. A slot holds its own copy of a pipeline or a soft pointer to a preset in another plugin's
  content; a preset from a plugin that is not installed is named, not an error. Choosing a workflow
  copies it into the definition, so editing one afterwards changes neither. The Stages tab picks,
  reapplies and saves them, and says what has changed since the workflow was applied. A new
  definition asks which workflow to start from, the project default first. Three ship with the
  plugin: *Generate from a prompt*, *Generate from your own picture* and *Edit a mesh in Blender*.
- **Stages can be switched off** per definition. A definition that starts from your own picture does
  not need Concept, one that starts from a mesh you already have does not need Concept, References
  or Mesh, and one whose takes you want to review first does not need Import. A switched-off stage is
  hidden from the Stages tab and the Settings tab, refused by every tool and left out of staleness.
  Every definition made before this keeps all five on and is not marked stale.
- A Mesh Definition's Content Browser tile shows what it made — its newest mesh, skinned or static —
  or, before anything is made, its main image, instead of the same icon on every definition. The
  thumbnail is stored in the asset and survives a restart: the mesh it shows is finished building before
  it is drawn, so it is never saved empty.
- `MeshForge.RebuildThumbnails [folder]` (and the Rebuild Definition Thumbnails agent tool) regenerates
  and saves every definition's thumbnail, and says which have nothing to show.
- A post step can start from **a step's output**: choose the step, then its latest run or any
  particular earlier run. Try a step with different settings, then carry on from the run you liked
  rather than the last one. Latest run inside a chain uses that chain's result. The default is
  unchanged and now reads "Step above, latest run".
- A **Floor** checkbox in the Mesh tab, off by default: most generated meshes keep their pivot at
  their centre, and the floor cut through the middle of them. The choice is remembered per user.
- **Edit in Blender - round trip**, a post step you finish by hand. It opens the mesh in Blender
  with any reference meshes locked beside it and a MeshForge tab in the sidebar. The chain waits
  until you press *Send back to Unreal*, then imports your edit as the step's output, restores the
  input's materials and carries on. A result sent after you stopped waiting, or while the editor was
  closed, can be picked up from the step. Blender's location is a per-user setting.
- Other plugins can add post steps without depending on MeshForge. A plugin registers a step — a
  settings class and a function — through `MeshForgeExtensions.h`, a header-only interface, and it
  appears under "From other plugins" in the Post stage's step picker. A definition opened without
  that plugin keeps the step and says which plugin it needs. A setting the plugin adds later and marks
  `SignatureOmitsDefault` does not mark existing steps stale.
- A step a person finishes can do its work inside the editor and hand back the edited asset itself.
  The chain records that asset as the step's output with nothing exported or imported again, so its
  vertex order, materials and build settings are kept. MeshForge Garment's in-editor garment sculpt
  is the first such step.
- **Edit in Blender works on a skinned mesh** as well as a static one. *Edit skinned mesh* on the step
  sends the skeletal mesh out with its skeleton, weights and morph targets, and brings back a copy of
  that same asset with its vertices moved to where Blender left them - nothing is imported, so the
  skeleton it is bound to, its weights, its morph targets and its materials are untouched. The topology
  has to come back unchanged, and the step says so, with both counts, when it does not. With the setting
  on the step works on assets, so it may follow a skinning step.
- An agent can work a step a person finishes one command at a time, through the step's
  `HandleInteractiveCommand` and MeshForge Toolset's Send Interactive Step Command. A step that runs to
  completion but has a window of its own takes commands too (`TakesCommands`), with or without a session
  (`CommandsNeedSession`).
- A post step can run on its own edit of its input instead of the input itself (`GetEditedInput`, asked
  on the game thread before the export). MeshForge Garment's Garment Studio keeps its sculpt this way.
- What belongs to one definition rather than to how things are made, such as a step's last session or an
  edit of its input, is left behind when a step is saved into a workflow and kept when a workflow is
  reapplied to the same definition (`ForgetDefinitionState`, `KeepDefinitionState`).

### Changed
- **A generator's pictures sit at the top of its settings**, straight under the prompt, instead of
  below every texture and shape setting. They are the first thing anybody checks. A post step keeps
  its own Input where it was.
- **A generator can say whether it builds from words or from a picture**, and the whole definition
  follows it: the settings show the prompt *or* the pictures, the Mesh stage asks for whichever is
  missing, the price quoted is the price of that request, and the take records only what was sent.
  Tripo is the first to offer the choice (`EMeshPipelineInput`, `UMeshForgePipeline::GetInputMode`).
  A generator that does not offer one behaves exactly as before.
- **A post step can start from a particular take of the Mesh stage.** *A step's output* listed only
  other post steps, so the first step - the one most likely to want a particular mesh - was told
  there were no steps to start from, even with a mesh freshly generated. The Mesh stage is now first
  in that list, and its finished takes are its runs: *Selected take* follows the Takes tab, or pick
  one and it stays that one. The take record names the take that was actually used, and List Post
  Inputs gives agents the same takes.
- A post step's **Advanced** actions now sit under the settings they work on, with Input and Pipeline
  after them, rather than above everything. The wardrobe skinning step put its *Sculpt in pose...*
  button above the Target Character it opens.
- **Each prompt belongs to the stage that reads it.** There is no longer one prompt above the stages:
  the Concept image stage's image pipeline has the words it draws from, the Mesh stage's generator the
  words it builds from where its provider reads text, and a retexture keeps its Style Prompt. A prompt
  shows only where it is read, first in that pipeline's settings; a definition that starts from a mesh
  shows none. Switching provider keeps a stage's prompt, and workflows keep the definition's prompts
  and never store their own. Existing definitions have their one prompt copied into their image and
  mesh pipelines when they load, and no stage goes stale.
- **The Stages tab reads at a glance.** Each stage is a box that opens and closes, numbered among the
  stages the definition uses (a definition that starts from a mesh no longer shows 4 and 5 after three
  stages it does not have), with a badge for where it stands and its status in the header. A stage
  that has run starts closed. Each post step is its own box inside Post-processing, with its last run in
  the header. A stage that has run and is up to date now says "done" rather than "ready".
- Post steps that make assets instead of geometry can now follow one another. The rule used to be
  "skeletal wardrobe creation must be last"; it is now "nothing that works on geometry may come after
  a step that makes an asset", so a skinned garment can be turned into an inventory item in the same
  chain.
- A post step's selected input can be a skeletal mesh, for steps that work on one.

### Fixed
- **A contradictory generator setting is now refused on the agent route too, before it spends.** The
  Stages tab has always checked a mesh pipeline before offering to run it, but the toolset came in
  further down and submitted regardless — so an agent could pay for a setting the vendor quietly
  ignores. The check now sits where both routes converge. Found by paying for it.
- **A post step no longer loses track of what made the mesh.** The chain used to overwrite the
  provenance after *every* step, so it answered "what ran last" rather than "what made this" — after
  a garment fit, a shirt genuinely generated on Tripo reported that it had not come from Tripo. The
  originating vendor task is now carried separately and only written by a step that actually returns
  one.
- **And it no longer offers a shortcut that would throw work away.** A vendor retextures the copy
  *it* holds and hands back its own geometry, which is free and correct while that copy is still our
  mesh — and silent data loss the moment it is not: point a wrapped garment at its originating task
  and back comes the *unwrapped* mesh, beautifully textured, with the wrap gone. A step that moves
  vertices now says so (`FMeshPipelineIO::bChangesGeometry`, on by default), the chain remembers it,
  and `UMeshPostPipeline::CanUseVendorTask` is the one place that decides. Getting it wrong in the
  safe direction costs an upload; getting it wrong the other way costs the work.

### Compatibility
- Update the MeshForge add-ons with it: MeshForgeCloud 0.3.0, MeshForgeTrellis 0.0.3, MeshForgeGarment
  0.2.0 and their toolsets. Their earlier builds were compiled against the previous MeshForge and are
  not compatible with this one.
- Packaging fix: the release now carries everything the register allows. `BuildPlugin`'s filter excludes `Config/` and every `public_extra` path, so earlier zips shipped without them.

- Documented that quads do not survive Unreal's Interchange import, and where they still exist for reference.
- Updated Tripo documentation to match the shipped v3 vendor surface.
- Repointed every plugin's Docs/Support URLs at kovati.dev.
- Added the garment pipeline: a generated shirt placed onto a MetaHuman, and the runner learning what a "body" is.
- Added a garment generated from the character's own picture (placed rather than fitted).
- Added Unreal-side inpainting as a separate skeletal post step.
- Added independent post-step execution with selectable saved inputs.
- Fixed healing of a definition that was saved while a job was in flight.
- Merged SurfaceForge (PR #4).

- Initial release: the mesh pipeline (prompt/image → provider → glTF → static mesh), Meshy and TRELLIS.2 as providers, image generation as its own pipeline stage with a gallery, per-take provenance vault, retexture as the first post pass, and the staged Mesh Definition panel (Stages/Images/Mesh/Settings).
- Fixed convex decomposition voxelising at 100 (always returning one hull) and corrected Meshy's image pricing.
- Moved HTTP polling off the game thread so drawing/generating no longer freezes the editor.
- Declared per-provider options (`FMeshControl::Extra`) so vendor-specific settings don't collide with the shared control struct.
- Split MeshForge Cloud out to ask for its own keys; documented that a key belongs to the plugin that spends it.

### Added
- **Aholo Lux3D, a third hosted provider.** Mesh generation on `G1` and `G1-Turbo` - from one
  picture, from up to 32 views (`imgs`), or from words with a `style` - with `faceCount`,
  `enablePbr`, `aiPredictSize` and `customSize` under the vendor's own names. G1-Turbo is listed at
  1 credit (about 1.5 cents), the cheapest mesh in the plugin by far. Its key goes on the Keys page
  beside Meshy's and Tripo's.
- **Two Lux3D picture pipelines**: `multimodal-to-image` for a reference picture from words, a
  picture or both, and `image-to-four-view`, which turns one picture into four views of the same
  object for multi-view reconstruction.
- **Two Lux3D post steps that work on any mesh**, a Meshy or Tripo take or one modelled in the
  project: `mesh-retopology` (a face budget, quad edge flow, and a bake of base colour, metallic and
  roughness) and `material-transfer` (repaint from a picture).
- **Tripo Texture v3.5**, on both Tripo steps. The generators gain **texture_version**, which pins
  the texture model independently of the model that builds the shape; the retexture step gains the
  same choice as **model**, where it had v3.0 hard-coded. Left alone both are unsent and the vendor
  derives them, so an existing definition keeps producing exactly what it produced.
- **`delight`** - take the reference picture's own lighting out before painting from it, on by the
  vendor's default. Read only by v3.5, so it is greyed out and unsent on the older texture models
  rather than left looking applied.
- **`texture_quality: fast`** - the fastest tier, same texture size and **the same credits** as
  standard; what it buys is time. It exists only on v3.5, and asking for it elsewhere is refused
  here - by the step and again by the provider - because Tripo refuses it too rather than painting
  at standard and charging for it. The retexture step's cost line now names the tier and the texture
  model it will send.

### Compatibility
- Needs MeshForge 0.3.2 for `material-transfer` to paint from the definition's main picture. A picture

### Known issues
- Lux3D has no seed, and its generation, retopology bake and material transfer return no normal map.
- Pictures and meshes are uploaded to Aholo, whose terms allow model training on uploads and generated
  outputs. Read its terms before sending work you cannot share; the README summarizes them.

### Added
- **meshy-7.1**, and it is the new default for the Standard pipeline. Same fields and the same price
  as meshy-7, with finer geometry; the vendor has deprecated meshy-7 and now resolves `latest` to
  7.1. A definition that names meshy-7 keeps naming it, and it still runs. **meshy-6-lite** is
  offered too, because the vendor accepts it — untested here.
- **`geometry_resolution`** — `standard`, `2k` or `4k` — replacing `ultra_mode`, which Meshy
  deprecated. It is how finely the *shape* is reconstructed and is easy to confuse with
  `texture_resolution`, which is unchanged and separate. `standard` is what `ultra_mode: false`
  gave and `2k` is what `ultra_mode: true` gave, so a saved definition is carried across to `2k` on
  load and keeps producing what it produced. 2k and 4k cost the same five extra credits; **4k needs
  meshy-7.1 or latest and a single picture**, and asking for it elsewhere is refused with the reason
  rather than sent. Measured why that matters: Meshy accepted `4k` on meshy-6 without a word of
  complaint, produced a mesh, and charged for the run — a setting silently dropped is worse than one
  refused.
- **Tripo can retexture a mesh it did not make.** It used to refuse one outright and tell you to go
  and use the Meshy step instead. `POST /v3/files` takes a `.glb` by the same plain multipart the
  plugin already used for pictures, and `/v3/models/texture` accepts the token it returns — the
  endpoint says so itself when refused: *"must be a valid task_id (UUID), file_token, or URL"*. So a
  CC5 shirt, a kitbash, a corridor somebody modelled all retexture on Tripo now, for the same 10
  credits. Measured: a 0.4 MB upload, textured in about a minute. An older note in this family held
  that our own meshes needed Tripo's STS route and therefore an AWS SigV4 signer; that was true of

**The first release.** SkinForge stamps scars, tattoos, wounds, implants, face paint and skin
detail onto a character as layers, previews them live on its own materials, then bakes them into
new copies of its textures and new material instances. The originals are never edited. Every bake
is a named version, and Apply and Revert switch a character, its Blueprints and its placed actors
between versions. A starter library of 60 marks in five packs comes with it.

SkinForge is a paid product with a free Lite tier, in one download.

### Added
- **Lite and Full.** Without a licence SkinForge runs as Lite, free: every baked map is at most
  2K (2048 on its longer side), a glow map too, and Upscale Base Color is shown greyed and marked
  "Full". With a licence that includes SkinForge it runs as Full: maps are baked at their source
  size, and Upscale Base Color enlarges base colour to 4K or 8K. Nothing else differs, and nothing
  is watermarked. The panel shows the tier under the Bake button, and a Lite bake says it once in
  its notes, which the Bake Skin Set and Stamp Skin Patch tools return.
- **How the tier is decided.** SkinForge reads the signed licence the Kovati Hub keeps on this
  computer. Sign in to the Hub with an account that owns SkinForge and it runs as Full; signed out,
  or without SkinForge in the licence, it runs as Lite. The licence keeps working offline for 30
  days after the Hub last refreshed it. Full is bought at
  [kovati.dev](https://kovati.dev/plugins/skinforge/). `SkinForge.Tier.ForceLite 1` runs a
  licensed copy as Lite, for testing.
- Everything the development history below describes, as its latest section leaves it.

### Compatibility
- **Unreal Engine 5.8, Windows (Win64), editor only.** Installed through the Kovati Hub.
- **SkinForgeToolset 0.3.1**, the free, open-source agent toolset, pairs with this version.

  re-assembly in MetaHuman Creator.

### Known issues
- **An apply to a MetaHuman placed in a level lasts until its construction script runs again**

  apply report says so. To keep a version on a character, apply it to its Blueprint or its assets.
- **A wrapped band round a limb reaches about 80° each side of its centre.** A full ring needs two

- **A set's first glowing bake compiles a copy of the skin material in the background.** Until it

- **Experimental.** File formats, settings and saved data may change between versions. Keep

### Added
- **Glowing marks come in a colour.** LED, UV circuit and the lit barcode now have a Colour choice:
  cyan-teal (the default), magenta or amber. The glow spills a few millimetres onto the skin round
  it, and the part under the skin is darker, so the mark still reads when the light is off. The
  LED cores are at full brightness.
- **`SkinForge::RenderReady(Set, Version)`**, for scripts. It says whether a version's baked
  materials are compiled, its textures built and its glow maps resident, and lists what is still
  pending. Poll it before taking a picture.

### Changed
- **Scars and wounds remade from clinical photographs** in the starter library:
  - **Cut, claw and surgical scars:** the line changes width along its length, is raised and
    puckered where it has healed, and the surgical scar shows its suture-track dots. The healed
    tissue reads on medium and dark skin, not only pale skin.
  - **Bullet and shrapnel scars** have a visible crater and pucker, with the skin pulled in round
    them and deeper height, so they read at a normal viewing distance.
  - **Graze** is less red and less busy: a wet raw patch, then a scab.
  - **Stab wound** is bigger and stronger.
  - **Bruise** is as strong as the black eye, with soft swelling. On Day 4 its edge turns
    yellow-green round a purple core.
  - **Fresh cigarette burns and burn blisters** have uneven raw centres that look wet and dark, not
    rings that glow.
  - **Staples** are visible steel: grey-silver, shiny and raised, about 6 mm across.
- **Small marks have twice the texture resolution.** Jacks, acne, bullet and shrapnel scars,
  cigarette burns and the small tattoos stay crisp up close.
- **A fresh tattoo is less glossy.** Its own Fresh roughness offset is now -0.05 (was -0.15).
- **Face paint and skin detail:**
  - **The Cracked look of the paints cracks and flakes.** Camo, finger stripes, mud, soot, blood smear and the war band dry into a network of fine cracks with flakes gone. Before, it barely changed, or showed smooth wavy lines.
  - **Camo** is matte olive, brown and black greasepaint with the pores showing through, and thin, uneven edges with no straight side.
  - **Finger stripes** are dragged and streaky, with dry gaps, in a darker red ochre.
  - **Mud** is a lighter grey-tan, so it shows on dark skin.
  - **Sweat** has beads, droplets and run trails that change only the shine and add a little relief. The orange stain on "Dripping" is gone.
  - **Freckles** have a Sun control from a winter dusting to dense, dark summer freckles.
  - **Sunburn** has a Strength control, from a blush to a deep red burn with a slight sheen and thin peeling.
- **Healed scars read on any skin.** The "Healed pale" look of the cut, claw, surgical and shrapnel scars is
  clearly paler than dark skin and a touch paler on fair skin. The healed tissue is smoother and slightly
  glossier, and stands a little proud or sunken. The fresh stages are unchanged.
- **The healing surgical scar** varies in width and has suture tracks across it and a broken-up tone.
- **The black eye on Day 4** keeps its purple in the lid crease and under the lashes, round it a mottled
  yellow-green that breaks up into the skin, with soft, irregular edges.
- **Summer freckles** are denser and darker across the nose and cheekbones.
- **The glowing barcode lights every bar evenly**, in all three colours. Before, thin bars glowed less, so
  part of the code looked dimmer.

### Fixed
- **A fresh tattoo's broad dark fills no longer glare like chrome.** The ointment film thins out to
  a quarter where the ink is dense, so a black fill reads as wet ink. It stays full on the red halo
  and on the skin between lines.
- **Glow now shows on a MetaHuman in every session.** 0.3.4's glow could vanish for two reasons:
  - **Its maps never streamed in after the editor restarted.** A glow map is named only by a
    material instance's override, so it had no streaming data: the editor kept its smallest mip
    and the glow averaged away. Glow maps are now always resident, about 11 MB for a 4K map.
    Re-bake older glow versions.
  - **The colour washed to pale pink or white.** A MetaHuman's skin is drawn through Unreal's
    subsurface pass, which took the glow with it and lost its colour, so cyan and amber looked the
    same. The glow copy now shades glowing texels as Default Lit, so the glow skips that pass under
    any `r.SSS.Checkerboard` setting, and darkens the skin under the glow by the glow's strength, as
    over an implant. Cyan, magenta and amber keep their colour. A skin with a fixed subsurface
    model divides the glow by its colour instead, which is right with checkerboard SSS on.
  - **The material copy compiled in the background.** A set's first glowing bake makes a copy of
    the skin material, and until its shaders finish the editor draws the skin without the glow.
    The bake still returns at once. Its notes now say which materials glow, from which copy and at
    what intensity, and whether shaders are still compiling. An editor notification stays up until
    they are done.

### Added
- **Glowing marks glow on a MetaHuman.** LED, UV ink and the lit barcode now light up on a baked
  MetaHuman. Before, its skin material had no emissive input, so the glow was dropped.
  - When a set has a glowing layer and the skin has no emissive texture, the bake writes a glow map
    beside the skin's colour map.
  - It also makes a copy of the skin's parent material, with an emissive input added
    ("SkinForge Emissive" and "SkinForge Emissive Intensity").
  - Copies of the material instances between that copy and the slot are made too, with their
    settings kept. All of these copies go in the set's `Glow` folder and are reused by later bakes.
  - The baked instance derives from those copies. The MetaHuman's own materials are never changed.
  - Sets without a glowing layer bake as before.
- **Glow Intensity**, on a skin set (under Bake, default 30, which reads as a lit mark under a low-key
  studio light; daylight scenes need more). It sets how bright that glow is. You can
  change it later on the baked instance.
- **Apply remakes a glowing face's per-actor instances.** A MetaHuman Blueprint makes per-actor
  material instances for its face, and these cannot take the glow as they are. Apply now remakes
  them from the glow version, keeping their own values, and Revert makes them again from what they
  came from.

**TerrainForge Lite and Full.** One plugin, two tiers, in the same download. Without a licence it runs as Lite, free;
with a licence that includes TerrainForge it runs as Full, with no limits. This release ends the free preview: a copy
that was taken free during the preview runs as Lite from this version on. Full is bought at
[kovati.dev](https://kovati.dev/plugins/terrainforge/).

### Added
- **Lite.** Builds, landscape imports and asset exports of at most 1009 x 1009 samples over at most 2 km x 2 km, and
  every node, erosion included, on the CPU. Nothing else is limited and nothing is watermarked. A recipe over the
  limits is refused with one sentence that says why; it is never scaled down behind your back. Levels already in a
  project are not touched, but a take larger than 1009 cannot be imported again in Lite.
- **How the tier is decided.** TerrainForge reads the signed licence the Kovati Hub keeps on this computer. Signed in
  with a licence that includes TerrainForge, it runs as Full; signed out, or with a licence that does not include it,
  it runs as Lite, and the **World & biomes** panel says which tier is running and why. The licence keeps working
  offline for 30 days after the Hub last refreshed it. `TerrainForge.Tier.ForceLite 1` runs a licensed copy as Lite,
  for testing.
- **1 m levels at 1009 samples (1008 m)**, next to 2017 and 4033, so Lite can make a real-world level too.
- **RainShadow node.** It follows the air along a prevailing wind: slopes the wind climbs get more rain, the lee of a
  range gets less, and the air recovers with distance.
- **Natural outline** for Volcano, Crater, Plateau and Mountain: uneven bays in place of the same repeating petals and
  radial streaks.
- **Optional Erode and Hydraulic controls:** a drop budget per detail level, detail under cover, drop steering (CPU
  only) and a Hydraulic batch limit. All are off by default and leave results as they were.

### Changed
- **In Lite**, previews above 1009 run at 1009, the classic presets (8 km) open as the same terrain scaled to 2 km, the
  4K and 8K presets are marked Full, and new definitions start at 1009 over 2 km. The 2K and 4K quality choices,
  larger grids and sizes over 2 km stay visible, locked, with "Full" beside them. The map picker offers squares up to
  2 km at grid 257 or 513.
- **Erode is about 23 % faster on the CPU**, with identical results.
- **The alpine, island, canyon and lake presets were rebuilt** after scoring them against real terrain. A terrain
  regenerated from one of these presets will look different.

### Fixed
- **Agents get the reason.** Generate Terrain and Import New Level return why a build or an import could not start (a
  Lite limit, a graph error, an unsaved map, ...) in place of a general sentence, and Get Status's error says why the
  last build was refused. Export Assets says its reason once. The Export panel shows why an import was refused.
- **Create Definition From Preset creates nothing** when the preset cannot be opened in this tier.

### Compatibility
- **TerrainForgeToolset 0.1.1** pairs with this version. If you use the toolset, update both together: 0.1.0 was
  built against TerrainForge 0.1.0.

### Known issues
- The known issues of 0.1.0 below still apply.

**The first PREVIEW release.** Node-based terrain for Unreal Engine 5.8: build a terrain as a graph, preview any node
live, compute it on the GPU or the CPU, and import it as a World Partition landscape with paint layers, rivers and
lakes. Or start from a real place. TerrainForge is a paid plugin, free during the preview. Everything runs inside the
editor; it starts no other program.

### Added

#### Graph & nodes
- **A terrain graph editor.** A node library with search, a graph canvas with validation, a node inspector, and
  undo for every edit. Terrain Definition assets live under **Add → Automation Forge → TerrainForge**.
- **94 node types in nine groups.** Generate (noise, gradients, imported heightfields), Select (height, slope,
  curvature, aspect, relative height, occlusion, rock and soil maps), Shape (warps, blurs, terraces, curves, upscale
  detail), Layer (a seven-layer stack and 24 blend modes), Simulate, Landforms, Water, Color and Export.
- **Erosion and geology in metres and years.** Particle erosion with sediment transport, stream power with
  deposition and deltas, hydraulic, thermal, talus and wind erosion, glaciers with U-shaped valleys and cirques,
  rockfall and scree, gullies, valley fill, snow with avalanches, and a folded, faulted rock volume that erosion
  exposes.
- **Landforms you place.** Mountains, winding mountain ranges, ridgelines drawn in the layout view, canyons,
  volcanoes, craters, island outlines, dune fields, plateaus, lava flows and rock strata.
- **Your own data.** Import a heightmap or mask (PNG, TIFF, RAW or R16) as a source node, up to 16 per definition.
  Save and open a whole graph as a portable JSON project with its sources.
- **Named outputs.** Any node output can be exported as its own 16-bit map, including normal and ambient-occlusion
  maps for materials.

#### Preview & GPU
- **Live previews.** Select a node and the 3D Terrain viewer shows it, at a coarse size first and then in full, with
  drainage water if you want it.
- **GPU compute, built in.** Blur, flow accumulation, particle erosion (with the rock volume), scree, and the parallel
  droplets of Hydraulic and Weathering run on a DirectX 12 GPU. The default policy, Auto, uses the GPU where a node
  has a kernel and the CPU elsewhere. A kernel that cannot run falls back to the CPU on its own.
- **Measured speed.** On an RTX 5080 Laptop GPU, a full 4033 build of the 4 km alpine preset took 79 s with Auto
  against 233 s on the CPU alone. Other machines differ.
- **Builds that reuse work.** A build runs the passes Base, Geology, Detail, Water and Maps, and reuses every pass
  whose inputs did not change. Results are the same for any number of CPU threads.
- **Memory you control.** Working-memory and GPU-memory budgets, a node cache, spill to disk, and an estimate of a
  build's memory before you start it.
- **A Build monitor.** Per-node progress, the device each node ran on, memory, time left, the maps written, and the
  last 12 builds of each definition.
- **Takes you keep.** Every build is saved as a take that is never overwritten: 16-bit heightmaps, paint weights
  that sum to 255, slope, aspect, flow, wetness, deposition, snow and moisture maps, biome and PCG masks, water
  outlines and meshes, a preview and a validation report.

#### World & landscape import
- **Import as new level.** A take becomes a new World Partition map with the landscape, paint layers and layer infos,
  a generated landscape material, engine water bodies for lakes and rivers, and a sun, sky and fog. It never writes
  over an existing map.
- **Large maps.** Output sizes from 1009 to 16321 samples. The editor imports up to 8129 samples, with Nanite up to
  4033, and a memory guard refuses an import that would not fit.
- **Headless import for the largest maps.** The `TerrainForgeImport` commandlet builds the landscape one streaming
  proxy at a time. A 16321 take with 8 paint layers and 56 water bodies imported with a peak of about 7.7 GB in our
  test, editor start-up included. `-VerifyLevel` checks a saved map against its take at every vertex.
- **Export bundles.** Bind take files to Landscape layers, PCG masks or textures, validate them, and write a Terrain
  Export Bundle asset with the textures, layer infos and hand-off files.

#### Rivers, lakes & biomes
- **Water three ways.** Draw rivers with per-point widths and branching junctions, place lakes at a chosen level, or
  let drainage route rivers and fill lakes from the terrain.
- **Water-shaped terrain.** River channels sized by their discharge, floodplains and terraces, lake shores with
  beaches, rocky benches and reed shelves, a sea level with cliffs and beaches, and a hydrology fix that makes every
  basin drain.
- **Biomes.** Temperate, arid and alpine biome presets turn height, slope, moisture, snow and water into paint layers
  and PCG masks. Treeline and snowline can follow the map's relief.

#### Maps & GIS
- **A map in the editor.** Search places offline or online, paste coordinates or map links, show relief, see which
  elevation source covers a square best, and see the landscape components and streaming proxies a square becomes.
  Quick 3D shows a square at about 30 m before you import.
- **Discover and import real terrain.** Ten elevation sources (France ×2, Switzerland, the United States, Norway, the
  Netherlands, England, North Rhine-Westphalia, and Copernicus and Terrain Tiles worldwide), ESA WorldCover land
  cover and 14 OpenStreetMap feature sets. Import the elevation plus up to 15 masks into a new graph or an existing
  one, for squares from 500 m to 50 km.
- **Fast once downloaded.** A 4033 import with 12 masks takes 2 to 3 seconds from cached data on a 24-thread CPU.
  Downloading usually takes longer and depends on the providers.
- **Attribution recorded for you.** Every import stores each dataset's source, licence and credit line in the
  definition. An export of OpenStreetMap vectors (`gis_vectors.geojson`) writes the ODbL notice beside it.
- **No accounts or keys for data.** Every elevation, land-cover and OpenStreetMap source is public. Optional map
  layers from Esri, MapTiler, Stadia, Thunderforest and Mapbox take your own key.

#### Level projects
- **Check location.** Test a square against a requirement profile: each requirement is covered by real data, partly
  covered, or replaced by a generated fill. The verdict is ready, ready with fills, or not recommended.
- **Create level project.** Build a 1 m level grid at 2017 or 4033 samples from the checked data and its fills, in
  about 5 seconds at 4033 from cached data on a 24-thread CPU. Undo restores the previous graph.
- **The `game_level` profile.** Elevation and eleven land requirements, painted into eight layers (Snow, Rocks, Scree, Meadow, Wetland,
  Soil, Forest, Water) with drainage water.
- **Your own profiles.** JSON files in `<Project>/Config/TerrainForge/GISProfiles`, or in folders you add in the
  settings, add profiles or replace a shipped one.

#### Agents & MCP
- **TerrainForgeToolset**, a free Apache-2.0 companion plugin: 44 typed MCP tools over the editor's own API, from
  presets and graph edits to builds, GIS, level projects, export and level import, with eight native agent skills.
- **Blueprint and editor scripting.** The subsystems and the preset library are callable from Blueprint and editor
  scripts.

#### Presets
- **18 presets.** Two eroded alpine presets (4 km at 4033 and 8 km at 8129) and 16 more: alpine ridges, layered and
  authored canyons, coastal and volcanic islands, placed mountains, dunes and mesa, a weathered massif and canyon,
  alpine materials, drawn river water, a crater lake, branching and widening rivers, talus breakdown and a wind-worn
  desert.
- **A preset picker with thumbnails**, from the Content Browser, the **Start from preset** toolbar button, Blueprint
  or the toolset.

### Compatibility
- **Unreal Engine 5.8, Windows (Win64), editor only.** TerrainForge turns on the engine's Water and Procedural Mesh
  Component plugins.
- **A DirectX 12 GPU (Shader Model 5 or later)** for GPU compute. Without one every node runs on the CPU.
- **Internet only for the map and GIS.** Graph editing, previews, builds and imports work offline.
- **TerrainForgeToolset 0.1.0** pairs with this version.

### Known issues
- **Builds do not survive an editor restart.** A build stops when the editor closes and cannot be reconnected. Build
  again.
- **Seam normals after a headless import.** Normals on streaming-proxy seams can differ by up to 106 of 255 on steep
  slopes until the editor's next edit-layer merge. The engine blends them at runtime.
- **Slow water saves.** Each water body takes 3 to 70 seconds to save during an import.
- **Plain first materials.** The generated landscape material uses flat layer colours, and water uses the engine's
  default materials.
- **Edge streaks in biomes.** With the default moisture setting, Forest, Meadow and Soil can streak on smooth slopes
  near the map edges. `moisture_wetness: mfd` removes them; the alpine presets use it.
- **A busy OpenStreetMap server.** The public Overpass server is shared and is sometimes busy. Imports wait and retry,
  and say so in their notes. You can add your own server in the TerrainForge GIS settings.
- **UK and Netherlands datum.** Elevation there is placed to about 2 m and 1 m, because the national datum grids are
  not applied.
- **A preview.** File formats, settings and saved data may change between versions. Keep backups.

**The first release**, alongside the TerrainForge 0.1.0 preview. Agent access to TerrainForge through Unreal Engine
5.8's toolset registry and MCP.

### Added
- **44 typed tools** over the same API the TerrainForge editor uses: definitions and presets, graph editing with
  revision checks, node previews, raster and project import, builds, GIS discovery and import, requirement profiles,
  location checks, level projects, export bindings and import into a new level.
- **Asynchronous results** for the long calls (builds, previews, imports, GIS jobs), typed like every other result.
- **Eight native agent skills**: authoring, generation, import, water, troubleshooting, graph editing, GIS and
  export. They are discovered automatically.
- **Safe by design.** No tool deletes a definition, a take or a map, overwrites a level, or writes a credential.

### Compatibility
- **Unreal Engine 5.8, editor only.**
- **Needs TerrainForge 0.1.0** and the engine's ToolsetRegistry plugin. An MCP client connects through the engine's
  Model Context Protocol plugin.
- **The GIS tools need internet access** to the data providers. Every other tool works offline.
